sections.overview: The Javan kingfisher is an Indonesian endemic known from Java and Bali.
sections.identification: This medium-sized bird is about 25 cm long, with a dark brown head, purple-blue body, bright blue wings, a red bill and legs, and a white wing patch visible in flight.
sections.habitat: It uses open woodland, scrub, fields, gardens, ponds, and other lowland habitats, including places near but not directly over water.
sections.diet: Its recorded prey include insects and other small animals such as fish, prawns, and frogs.
sections.behavior: It is mainly solitary, strongly territorial, and sedentary, staying close to its nesting area.
sections.reproduction: It nests in a tunnel excavated in an exposed earthen bank; reports give three or four white eggs, with breeding recorded from March to September.
sections.ecology: Its broad prey and use of both wet and dry habitats make it less dependent on aquatic prey than many familiar kingfishers.
sections.conservation: The cited Indonesian species account reports the IUCN category as Least Concern; detailed population trends were not provided there.
